full_judgment:
Md Fazlul Karim J : This appeal by leave arises out of impugned judgment and order dated 8-3-2000 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 2154 of 2000 arising out of CR Case No. 130 of 1999 corresponding to Petition Case No. 1572 of 1998 in the Court of Magistrate, 1st Class, Combined Criminal Court, 'Ka' Anchal, Gaibandha. 

 2. The case arose out of a complaint at the instance of one Md. Hasan Karim, Director of Raqib Food Industries Private Limited at DB Road, Gaibandha on September 17, 1998 who lodged the same in the Court of Magistrate, 1 st Class, Combined Criminal Court, 'Ka' Anchal, Gaibandha alleging, inter alia, that at the instigation of the accused Nos. 3 and 4 the complainant established a company namely, Raqib Food Industries Pvt Ltd at Gaibandha and the same was registered duly by the Registrar of Joint Stock Companies and the accused appellant No.1 was made Managing Director and the accused appellant No.2 was made one of the Directors of the Board of Directors; that on 15-9-1993, a cheque amounting to Taka 42,093 was issued from the Rupali Bank at Rangpur Branch as part of the loan and the accused appellant without submitting the cheque to the account of the Raqib Food Industries deposited in his personal Account No. 921 with Rupali Bank at Gaibandha Branch vide DD 22/21 No. 578294 dated 17-9-1993 and misappropriated the same; that another cheque from Rupali Bank, Rangpur Branch dated 20-9-1993 amounting to Taka 1,25,193 in favour of the said Raqib Food Industries, the accused-appellant without depositing the same to the account of the Raqib Food Industries, deposited Taka 1,25,000 in his personal current account No. 11 with Rupali Bank, Gaibandha Branch vide DD 22/26 No. 578294 dated 23-9-1993 and misappropriated the same and thus all the accused committed offence under sections 406/420/34 of the Penal Code. 

 3. The accused-appellants after being informed on January 13, 2000 appeared before the Magistrate and filed application for bail and the Court below by the order dated 13-1-2000 granted bail to the accused appellants. That since the allegation of misappropriation of money belonged to the Raqib Food Industries Pvt. Ltd. and the accused appellant No.1 being Managing Director and the accused-appellant No.2 one of the Directors of the said Company, the complainant as one of the Directors of the said Company could not file any criminal case for misappropriating the money of the Company the appellant filed an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashing the proceeding. 

 "From the allegations, we find clear breach of trust having been committed by the accuseds and, inasmuch as they misappropriation the money, on several occasions, as detailed in the petition of complaint and the amount also a heavy one. The breach of trust and misappropriation have been committed by the accuseds in connivance with one another and the accuseds are very near relatives. We cannot consider the defence case sitting under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The truth will come out in the trial after adducing of evidence by the parties in the trial Court. However, from our meticulous reading of the petition of complaint, we find prima facie cases having been established under sections 406/420 of the Penal Code. So, the accuseds should face trial and, in view of the facts and circumstances, we are not inclined to quash the proceedings." 

 7. Mr Mansur Habib, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellants, submitted that in view of the fact that the appellant being admittedly the Managing Director and a director of the company of which the complainants are directors and in the course of official business are alleged to have issued cheques which amount was allegedly misappropriated by the appellants, could not be legally termed as misappropriation or breach of trust of the fund of the company for a criminal prosecution under sections 406/420 of the Penal Code and that the remedy, if there be any, is one of accounting and mesne profit for which a civil suit for accounts is the appropriate remedy and hence the prosecution of the appellant under sections 406/420 of the Penal Code is not maintainable per' se and accordingly, is liable to be quashed. The learned Advocate has referred to the decisions in the case of Nasiruddin Mahmud and others vs Momtazuddin Ahmed and another reported in 1984 BLD (AD) 97 and Md Yameen and another vs KA Bashar and others reported in 1986 BLD (AD) 305 for the above proposition. 

 9. In the case of Nasiruddin Mahmud and others vs Momtazuddin Ahmed and another reported in 1984 BLD (AD) 97, the question arose as to whether the partner can be charged by his co- partner with an offence for the breach of trust and cheating under sections 406/420 of the Penal Code in respect of partnership business entrusting the money for the purpose, wherein it was held reviewing the decisions on the subject that a partner could not be alleged to be misappropriated or cheated when an amount was entrusted to the accused for the partnership business. 

 10. Similar view has been taken in the case Md Yameen and another vs KA Bashar and others reported in 1986 BLD (AD) 305 and the issue was as to whether the Managing Director and Chairman of a company, the trustees of the fund of the company, could be prosecuted for misappropriation of the fund of the company and as to whether the principle of law applicable to the members of the partnership shall apply to the private limited company for the proposition that the directors of the company are trustees of the money of the business in their hands and control and they could not be prosecuted for misappropriation of fund and cheating the other directors and accordingly, the prosecution against one director by another for alleged misappropriation and cheating was quashed. 

 11. The facts and circumstances of the cited decisions apply with all force in the instant case. Accordingly, we find merit in the submissions of the learned Counsel for the appellant.
